A smooth sphere S is moving on a smooth horizontal plane with speed \(u\) when it collides with a smooth fixed vertical wall. At the instant of collision the direction of motion of S makes an angle of 60\(^{\circ}\) with the wall. The coefficient of restitution between S and the wall is \(\frac{1}{4}\). Find:\par (a) The speed of S immediately after the collision\par (b) The angle of deflection of S

(a) Parallel to the smooth wall the velocity component is unchanged: \(v\cos\beta=u\cos60^\circ\). Perpendicular to it, the rebound component is \(v\sin\beta=\tfrac14u\sin60^\circ\).\par Square and add: \(v^2=u^2/4+3u^2/64=19u^2/64\). Thus \(v=\sqrt{19}u/8\).
(b) Divide the perpendicular equation by the parallel equation. Then \(\tan\beta=\tfrac14\tan60^\circ\), giving \(\beta=23.4^\circ\). The deflection is \(60^\circ+23.4^\circ=83.4^\circ\) (1 d.p.).
Edexcel M4 · June 2015 · Question 7a

Figure 4 represents the plan view of part of a smooth horizontal floor, where AB and BC are smooth vertical walls. The angle between AB and BC is \(120^\circ\). A ball is projected along the floor towards AB with speed u \(m{s}^{-1}\) on a path at an angle of 60° to AB. The ball hits AB and then hits BC. The ball is modelled as a particle. The coefficient of restitution between the ball and each wall is \(\frac{1}{2}\).\par Show that the speed of the ball immediately after it has hit AB is \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{4}\) u .\par

Parallel to the first wall: \(v\cos\theta=u\cos60^\circ=u/2\). Normal to it: \(v\sin\theta=\tfrac12u\sin60^\circ=\sqrt3u/4\).\par Hence \(\tan\theta=\sqrt3/2\) and \(\theta=40.9^\circ\). Squaring and adding gives \(v^2=7u^2/16\), so \(v=\sqrt7u/4\).

A smooth sphere S is moving on a smooth horizontal plane with speed u when it collides with a smooth fixed vertical wall. At the instant of collision the direction of motion of S makes an angle of \(\alpha\) with the wall, where \(\tan \alpha=2\). Immediately after the collision the speed of S is \(\frac{3}{4}u\).\par Find the coefficient of restitution between S and the wall. [4 marks]

\(\tan \alpha = 2 \Rightarrow \cos \alpha = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\) and \(\sin \alpha = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\) (from Pythagoras' theorem)\par For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(\frac{3u}{4} \cos \beta = u \cos \alpha\) [M1]\par \(\frac{3u}{4} \cos \beta = \frac{u}{\sqrt{5}}\) (1)\par For motion perpendicular to the wall:\par \(\frac{3u}{4} \sin \beta = eu \sin \alpha\) [M1]\par \(\frac{3u}{4} \sin \beta = \frac{2eu}{\sqrt{5}}\) (2)
Squaring and adding equations (1) and (2) gives:

\(\frac{9}{16} u^2 (\cos^2 \beta + \sin^2 \beta) = u^2 \left( \frac{1}{5} + \frac{4e^2}{5} \right)\)\par \(\frac{45}{16} = 1 + 4e^2\)\par \(e^2 = \frac{29}{64} \Rightarrow e = \frac{\sqrt{29}}{8}\) [A1]

A small smooth ball of mass 750 g is falling vertically. The ball strikes a smooth plane which is inclined at an angle of \(45^{\circ}\) to the horizontal. Immediately before striking the plane the ball has speed \(5 \sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}\) The coefficient of restitution between the ball and the plane is \(\frac{1}{2}\). Find:\par \textbf{a)} the speed, to 3 significant figures, of the ball immediately after the impact [2 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the magnitude of the impulse received by the ball as it strikes the plane. [2 marks]\par Hint  \(\mathbf I=m\mathbf v-m\mathbf u\)\par ← Section 1.3

The component of velocity parallel to the slope is \(5\sqrt{2}\sin 45^{\circ}=5\sqrt{2}\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=5\)\par Perpendicular to the slope: \(v=\frac{1}{2}\times5\sqrt{2}\cos 45^{\circ}=\frac{1}{2}\times5\sqrt{2}\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{5}{2}=2.5\) [M1]\par Therefore the speed immediately after impact \(=\sqrt{5^{2}+2.5^{2}}=\sqrt{31.25}=5.59\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} The impulse is perpendicular to the surface:
\(\mathrm{I}=m v-m(-5\sqrt{2}\cos 45^{\circ})\) [M1]

A small smooth ball is falling vertically. The ball strikes a smooth plane which is inclined at an angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\tan \alpha=\frac{3}{4}\). transcription.tex: Question 16

A small smooth sphere of mass 2 kg is moving with velocity \(( 2 \mathbf{i}+3 \mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) when it hits a smooth wall. It rebounds from the wall with velocity \(( 3 \mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\). Find:\par \textbf{a)} the magnitude and direction of the impulse received by the sphere [3 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the coefficient of restitution between the sphere and the wall [5 marks]\par \textbf{c)} the kinetic energy lost by the sphere in the collision. [4 marks]

\textbf{a)} Impulse \(= mv - mu\)\par \(I = m(3i - j) - m(2i + 3j)\) [M1]\par \(I = 2(i - 4j)\) [A1]\par The impulse has magnitude \(2\sqrt{17} \text{ Ns}\) in the direction parallel to the unit vector \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j)\) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Component of \((2i + 3j)\) in the direction of the impulse

\(= \left[(2i + 3j).\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j)\right]\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(2 - 12)\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j) = -\frac{10}{17}(i - 4j)\) [M1] [A1]\par Component of \((3i - j)\) in the direction of the impulse

\(= \left[(3i - j).\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j)\right]\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(3 + 4)\frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}(i - 4j) = \frac{7}{17}(i - 4j)\) [A1]\par By Newton's law of restitution: [M1]

\(\frac{7}{17} = e \times \frac{10}{17} \Rightarrow e = \frac{7}{10} = 0.7\) [A1]\par \textbf{c)} Kinetic energy before impact \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (2^2 + 3^2) = 13\) [M1]\par Kinetic energy after impact \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (3^2 + 1^2) = 10\) [A1]\par Kinetic energy lost \(= 13 - 10 = 3\,\text{ J}\) [M1] [A1]

transcription.tex: Question 17

A sphere slides across a smooth horizontal plane towards a smooth vertical wall with a speed of \(3 v\) and at an angle of \(\alpha\) to the wall. After striking the wall the sphere moves at right-angles to its original direction of motion with speed \(v\).\par \textbf{a)} Show that \(\tan \alpha=3\) [3 marks]\par \textbf{b)} Find the coefficient of restitution between the sphere and the wall. [4 marks]

\textbf{a)} For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(\nu\cos(90^{\circ}-\alpha)=3\nu\cos\alpha\) [M1]\par \(\Rightarrow\sin\alpha=3\cos\alpha\) (as \(\cos(90^{\circ}-\alpha)=\sin\alpha)\) [A1]\par \(\Rightarrow\tan\alpha=3\) [A1]

\textbf{b)} Resolve normal to the wall. The speed of approach is \(3v\sin\alpha\) [M1], and the speed of separation is \(v\sin(90^\circ-\alpha)=v\cos\alpha\) [M1]. Restitution therefore gives \(e=v\cos\alpha/(3v\sin\alpha)=1/(3\tan\alpha)\) [A1]. Using part (a), \(e=1/9\) [A1].

transcription.tex: Question 18

A particle P is moving in a vertical plane when it collides with a smooth fixed horizontal wall. Immediately before the collision the angle between the direction of motion of P and the wall is \(\alpha\) where \(0^{\circ}<\alpha<90^{\circ}\). Immediately after the collision, the angle between the direction of motion of P and the wall is \(\frac{1}{2}\alpha\). Given that the coefficient of restitution between P and the wall is 0.4, find the value of \(\alpha\) [10 marks]

For motion parallel to wall:\par \(v \cos \frac{\alpha}{2} = u \cos \alpha\) (1) [M1] [A1]\par For motion perpendicular to wall:\par \(v \sin \frac{\alpha}{2} = eu \sin \alpha = 0.4u \sin \alpha\) (2) [M1] [A1]\par Dividing equation (2) by equation (1) gives:\par \(\tan \frac{\alpha}{2} = 0.4 \tan \alpha\) (3) [A1]\par Using the identity:
\(\tan(\theta + \phi) = \frac{\tan \theta + \tan \phi}{1 - \tan \theta \tan \phi}\) with \(\theta = \phi = \frac{\alpha}{2}\) [B1]
\(\tan \alpha = \frac{2 \tan \frac{\alpha}{2}}{1 - \tan^2 \frac{\alpha}{2}}\) [M1]\par Writing \(\tan \frac{\alpha}{2}\) as \(t\), and substituting into equation (3)

\(t = 0.4 \times \frac{2t}{1 - t^2}\) if \(t \neq 0\) [A1]\par \(1 - t^2 = 0.8\)\par \(t^2 = 0.2\) [A1]\par So \(t = \tan \frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{0.2}\)\par \(\Rightarrow \frac{\alpha}{2} = 24.09^\circ \Rightarrow \alpha = 48.2^\circ\) (3 s.f.) [A1]

transcription.tex: Two vertical walls meet at right angles. A smooth sphere slides across a smooth, horizontal floor, bouncing off each wall in turn. Just before the first impact the sphere is moving with speed 4\(m{s}^{-1}\) at an angle of 30\(^{\circ}\). The coefficient of restitution between the sphere and both walls is \(\frac{3}{4}.\) Find\par (a) The direction of motion and speed of the sphere after the first collision\par (b) The direction of motion and speed of the sphere after the second collision.
(a) At the first wall, \(v\cos\beta=4\cos30^\circ\) and \(v\sin\beta=\tfrac34(4\sin30^\circ)\). Divide to obtain \(\beta=23.4^\circ\). Square and add to obtain \(v=3.77\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

(b) The walls are perpendicular, so the approach angle to the second wall is \(90^\circ-\beta\). Its parallel component is \(w\cos\gamma=v\sin\beta=1.5\). Its normal rebound component is \(w\sin\gamma=\tfrac34v\cos\beta=3\sqrt3/2\). Thus \(w=3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(\gamma=60^\circ\) to the second wall.
Edexcel M4 · June 2015 · Question 7b

Figure 4 represents the plan view of part of a smooth horizontal floor, where AB and BC are smooth vertical walls. The angle between AB and BC is \(120^\circ\). A ball is projected along the floor towards AB with speed u m s–1 on a path at an angle of 60° to AB. The ball hits AB and then hits BC. The ball is modelled as a particle. The speed of the ball immediately after it has hit BC is w m s–1.\par The coefficient of restitution at each wall is \(1/2\). From part (a), the speed after the first collision is \(v=\sqrt7u/4\).\par (b)     Find w in terms of u.

The approach angle to the second wall is \(180^\circ-120^\circ-40.9^\circ=19.1^\circ\).\par Parallel: \(w\cos\phi=v\cos19.1^\circ\). Normal: \(w\sin\phi=\tfrac12v\sin19.1^\circ\).\par Squaring and adding gives \(w^2=v^2(\cos^219.1^\circ+\tfrac14\sin^219.1^\circ)\). Hence \(w=0.634u\) (3 s.f.).

Two smooth vertical walls stand on a smooth horizontal floor and intersect at an acute angle \(\theta \). A small smooth particle is projected along the floor at right angles to one of the walls and away from it. After one impact with each wall the particle is moving parallel to the first wall it struck. Given that the coefficient of restitution between the particle and each wall is \(e\) show that:
\(\left(1+2e\right){\tan }^{2} \theta ={e}^{2}\)

At X, resolving along and normal to the first wall gives \(u\sin\theta=v\cos\beta\) and \(eu\cos\theta=v\sin\beta\). Hence \(\tan\beta=e\cot\theta\). At Y the approach angle is \(\beta-\theta\) by alternate angles. Thus \(v\cos(\beta-\theta)=w\cos\theta\) and \(ev\sin(\beta-\theta)=w\sin\theta\).

Division gives \(e\tan(\beta-\theta)=\tan\theta\). Expand the tangent of the difference and substitute \(\tan\beta=e\cot\theta\):\par \(e(e\cot\theta-\tan\theta)/(1+e)=\tan\theta\).\par So \(e^2\cot\theta=(1+2e)\tan\theta\). Multiply by \(\tan\theta\) to obtain \((1+2e)\tan^2\theta=e^2\).

transcription.tex: Question 3

Two smooth vertical walls stand on a smooth horizontal surface and intersect at right angles.\par A smooth sphere of mass 0.1 kg is moving in the xy-plane such that it collides with the first wall at a speed of \(0.25\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) at an angle of \(30^{\circ}\) to the wall.\par The coefficient of restitution between the sphere and both walls is e. Given that after the first collision the sphere is moving with speed \(0.23\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\), work out:\par \textbf{a)} the direction in which the sphere is moving [2 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the value of e. [2 marks]\par The sphere then moves on to collide with the second wall.\par \textbf{c)} Calculate the kinetic energy of the sphere after the second collision. [6 marks]

\textbf{a)} First collision – let the angle the sphere makes with the wall after the collision be \(\alpha\)\par For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(0.23 \cos \alpha = 0.25 \cos 30^\circ\) [M1]\par (1)\par \(\cos \alpha = \frac{0.25}{0.23} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0.94133\ldots\)\par \(\Rightarrow \alpha = 19.7^\circ \text{ (3 s.f.)}\) [A1]\par After the impact with the first wall, the sphere moves at \(19.7^\circ\) to the wall
\textbf{b)} For motion perpendicular to the wall:
\(0.23 \sin \alpha = 0.25 e \sin 30^\circ\) [M1]\par (2)\par Dividing equation (2) by equation (1) gives:

\(\tan \alpha = e \tan 30^\circ\)\par \(\Rightarrow e = \frac{\tan \alpha}{\tan 30^\circ} = \frac{\tan 19.72^\circ}{\tan 30^\circ} = 0.621 \text{ (3 s.f.)}\) [A1]\par \textbf{c)} First collision – let the angle the sphere makes with the wall after the collision be \(\beta\) and its speed after the collision be \(v\)\par For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(v \cos \beta = 0.23 \cos(90^\circ - \alpha) = 0.23 \sin \alpha\) [M1]\par (3)\par For motion perpendicular to the wall:\par \(v \sin \beta = 0.23 e \sin(90^\circ - \alpha) = 0.23 e \cos \alpha\) [M1]\par (4)\par Squaring and adding equations (3) and (4) gives:

\(v^2 \cos^2 \beta + v^2 \sin^2 \beta = 0.23^2 \sin^2 \alpha + 0.23^2 e^2 \cos^2 \alpha\) [M1]\par \(v^2 (\cos^2 \beta + \sin^2 \beta) = 0.23^2 (1 - \cos^2 \alpha + e^2 \cos^2 \alpha)\)\par \(v^2 = 0.0529(1 - 0.94133^2 + 0.621^2 \times 0.94133^2) = 0.0241\ldots\) [A1]\par Kinetic energy after second collision \(= \frac{1}{2} mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times 0.0241 = 0.00121\,\text{ J (3 s.f.)}\) [M1] [A1]

transcription.tex: Question 4

Two smooth vertical walls, \(W_{1}\) and \(W_{2}\),stand on a smooth horizontal surface and intersect at right angles. A smooth ball of mass 2 kg is moving in the xy-plane such that it collides with the first wall at an angle of \(60^{\circ}\) to the wall. The coefficients of restitution between the ball and the walls \(W_{1}\) and \(W_{2}\) are 0.75 and 0.6 respectively. Given that immediately before the first collision the ball has kinetic energy of 9 J, work out:\par \textbf{a)} the speed and direction of motion of the ball after the first collision [4 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the kinetic energy of the ball after the second collision. [4 marks]

\textbf{a)} First collision – let the angle the sphere makes with the wall after the collision be \(\alpha\), its speed before impact be \(u\) and its speed after impact \(v_1\)\par Kinetic energy before first collision \(= \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times u^2\) [M1]\par So \(u^2 = 9 \Rightarrow u = 3 \text{ ms}^{-1}\)\par For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(v_1 \cos \alpha = 3 \cos 60^\circ = 1.5\) (1) [M1]\par For motion perpendicular to the wall:
\(v_1 \sin \alpha = 0.75 \times 3 \sin 60^\circ = 1.125\sqrt{3}\) (2) [M1]
Squaring and adding equations (1) and (2) gives:\par \(v_1^2 \cos^2 \alpha + v_1^2 \sin^2 \alpha = 2.25 + 3.7969\)

\(v_1^2 (\cos^2 \alpha + \sin^2 \alpha) = 6.0469\)\par \(v_1 = 2.46 \text{ ms}^{-1}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]\par Dividing equation (2) by equation (1) gives:\par \(\tan \alpha = 0.75 \tan 60^\circ = 0.75\sqrt{3}\)\par \(\Rightarrow \alpha = 52.4^\circ\) (3 s.f.)\par \textbf{b)} Second collision – for motion parallel to the wall:\par \(v_2 \cos \beta = v_1 \cos(90^\circ - \alpha) = v_1 \sin \alpha\) (3) [M1]\par For motion perpendicular to the wall:\par \(v_2 \sin \beta = 0.6v_1 \sin(90^\circ - \alpha) = 0.6v_1 \cos \alpha\) (4) [M1]\par Squaring and adding equations (3) and (4) gives:

\(v_2^2 \cos^2 \beta + v_2^2 \sin^2 \beta = v_1^2 \sin^2 \alpha + v_1^20.36 \cos^2 \alpha\) [M1]\par \(v_2^2 (\cos^2 \beta + \sin^2 \beta) = v_1^2 (\sin^2 \alpha + 0.36 \cos^2 \alpha)\)\par \(v_2^2 = 6.0469(0.6279 + 0.13395) = 4.60685\)\par Kinetic energy after second collision \(= \frac{1}{2} m v_2^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4.60685 = 4.61\,\text{ J}\) (3 s.f.) [A1]

transcription.tex: Question 7

Two vertical walls stand on a smooth horizontal surface and intersect at an angle of \(45^{\circ}\).\par A smooth sphere is projected across the surface with speed \(5\,\mathrm{~m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) at an angle of \(30^{\circ}\) to the first wall and towards the intersection of the walls. The coefficient of restitution between the sphere and both walls is 0.8. Work out the speed and direction of motion of the sphere after:\par \textbf{a)} the first collision [4 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the second collision. [4 marks]\par In reality the coefficients of restitution between the sphere and the first wall, \(e_{1}\), and the sphere and the second wall, \(e_{2}\), may not be the same.\par \textbf{c)} Without doing any further calculation, state how the speed and direction of motion of the sphere after the second collision would change if \(e_{2} > 0.8\) [1 mark]

\textbf{a)} First impact:\par For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(v_1 \cos \alpha = 5 \cos 30^\circ\) [M1]\par (1)\par For motion perpendicular to the wall:\par \(v_1 \sin \alpha = 0.8 \times 5 \sin 30^\circ\) [M1]\par (2)\par Squaring and adding equations (1) and (2) gives:\par \(v_1^2 \cos^2 \alpha + v_1^2 \sin^2 \alpha = 25 \times \frac{3}{4} + 16 \times \frac{1}{4}\)
\(v_1^2 = \frac{91}{4} \Rightarrow v = 4.77 \text{ ms}^{-1} \text{ (3 s.f.)}\) [A1]
Dividing equation (2) by equation (1) gives:

\(\tan \alpha = 0.8 \tan 30^\circ = \frac{4}{5\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \alpha = 24.8^\circ \text{ (3 s.f.)}\) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Second impact:\par For motion parallel to the wall:\par \(v_2 \cos \beta = v_1 \cos(45^\circ + \alpha)\) [M1]\par (3)\par For motion perpendicular to the wall:\par \(v_2 \sin \beta = 0.8v_1 \sin(45^\circ + \alpha)\) [M1]\par (4)\par Dividing equation (4) by equation (3) gives:\par \(\tan \beta = 0.8 \tan(45^\circ + \alpha) = 0.8 \tan(45^\circ + 24.791^\circ) = 2.1733\)\par \(\Rightarrow \beta = 65.3^\circ \text{ (3 s.f.)}\) [A1]

From equation (3):\par \(v_2 \cos 65.291^\circ = v_1 \cos(45^\circ + \alpha)\)\par \(v_2 = 4.77 \times \frac{\cos 69.791^\circ}{\cos 65.291^\circ} = 3.94 \text{ ms}^{-1} \text{ (3 s.f.)}\) [A1]\par \textbf{c)} If \(e_2 > 0.8\) and \(e_1\) remains unchanged, \((45^\circ + \alpha)\) and \(v_1\) do not change; however, \(\tan \beta\) increases, so \(\beta\) increases and \(v_2\) (which depends on \(v_1\) and \(\cos \beta\)) increases.\par So the velocity of the sphere after the second collision would be greater and the angle it makes with the wall after the collision would be greater. [B1]

transcription.tex: Question 8

Two smooth vertical walls stand on a smooth horizontal surface and intersect at right angles, parallel with the vectors i and j. A small smooth sphere of mass m is moving with velocity \(( 5 \mathbf{i}-4 \mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) when it hits one of the walls. It rebounds from the wall with velocity \(( 5 \mathbf{i}+2 \mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\) and goes on to hit the second wall. The coefficients of restitution between the sphere and each wall are the same. Find:\par \textbf{a)} the kinetic energy lost by the sphere in the collisions [5 marks]\par \textbf{b)} the total angle through which the sphere is deflected in its motion. [3 marks]

\textbf{a)} Since first collision causes no change to the \(i\) component, first collision must be with the wall parallel to this vector.\par Considering \(j\) components only for the first collision:\par \(2 = 4e \Rightarrow e = \tfrac12\) [M1] [A1]\par Considering only the \(i\) component changes for the second collision:\par \(p = 5e = \tfrac52 = 2.5\) [A1]\par Loss of kinetic energy \(= \frac{1}{2} m \left( |u|^2 - |v|^2 \right)\)
\(= \frac{1}{2} m \left( 41 - \frac{41}{4} \right)\)\par \(= \frac{123}{8} m\,\text{ J}\) [A1]\par \textbf{b)} Initial velocity, \(u = 5i - 4j\) and final velocity, \(v = -2.5i + 2j\) [M1]

The coefficients of \(i\) [M1] and \(j\) have the same ratio in both cases, but the signs of both are reversed: \(u\) and \(v\) are therefore antiparallel. The sphere is deflected through a total angle of \(180^\circ\) [A1].

transcription.tex: A small smooth sphere A of mass 1kg collides with a small smooth sphere B of mass 2kg. Just before the impact A is moving with a speed of 4\(m{s}^{-1}\) in a direction at \(45^{\circ}\) to the line of centres and B is moving with a speed 3\(m{s}^{-1}\) at 60\(^{\circ}\) to the line of centres, as shown in the diagram. The coefficient of restitution between the spheres is \(\frac{3}{4}. \) Find:\par (a) The kinetic energy lost in the impact\par (b) The magnitude of the impulse exerted by A on B

(a) Resolve along the line of centres. Write \(p=4\cos45^\circ\), \(q=3\cos60^\circ\). Momentum gives \(p-2q=x_A+2x_B\); restitution gives \(x_B-x_A=3(p+q)/4\). Thus \(x_A=-7/4-\sqrt2/3\), \(x_B=7\sqrt2/6-5/8\).\par Initial kinetic energy is \(\tfrac12(4^2)+3^2=17\,\mathrm J\). Final kinetic energy is \(\tfrac12[x_A^2+(4\sin45^\circ)^2]+x_B^2+(3\sin60^\circ)^2\). The loss is \(2.73\,\mathrm J\).
(b) Only the component along the line of centres changes. The magnitude of the impulse on B is \(2[x_B-(-3\cos60^\circ)]=5.05\,\mathrm{N\,s}\) (3 s.f.).

slides.title: Checking the energy loss using relative speed

transcription.tex: A small smooth sphere A of mass 1kg collides with a small smooth sphere B of mass 2kg. Just before the impact A is moving with a speed of 4\(m{s}^{-1}\) in a direction at \(45^{\circ}\) to the line of centres and B is moving with a speed 3\(m{s}^{-1}\) at 60\(^{\circ}\) to the line of centres, as shown in the diagram. The coefficient of restitution between the spheres is \(\frac{3}{4}. \) Find:\par (a) The kinetic energy lost in the impact\par (b) The magnitude of the impulse exerted by A on B

(a) Use the relative speed along the line of centres. Let \(g=4\cos45^\circ+3\cos60^\circ\). The reduced mass is \(\mu=(1)(2)/(1+2)=2/3\,\mathrm{kg}\). The translational energy of the centre of mass and the tangential energies are unchanged. The relative normal kinetic energy falls from \(\tfrac12\mu g^2\) to \(\tfrac12\mu(eg)^2\). Thus the loss is \(\tfrac12(2/3)(1-9/16)g^2=2.73\,\mathrm J\).
(b) The impulse changes the relative normal speed by \(J(1/m_A+1/m_B)=(1+e)g\). Hence \(J=\mu(1+e)g=(2/3)(7/4)g=5.05\,\mathrm{N\,s}\).

A smooth uniform sphere S, of mass m, is moving on a smooth horizontal plane when it collides obliquely with another smooth uniform sphere T, of the same radius as S but of mass 2m, which is at rest on the plane. Immediately before the collision the velocity of S makes an angle \(\alpha\), where tan \(\alpha=\frac{3}{4}\), with the line joining the centres of the spheres.\par Immediately after the collision the speed of T is V. The coefficient of restitution between the two spheres is \(\frac{3}{4}\).\par (a) Find, in terms of V, the speed of S\par (i) immediately before the collision,\par (ii) immediately after the collision.\par (b) Find the angle through which the direction of motion of S is deflected as a result of the collision.\par

(a) Let the initial speed of S be \(u\) and its final signed component along the centres be \(w\). Momentum gives \(u\cos\alpha=w+2V\). Restitution gives \(\tfrac34u\cos\alpha=V-w\). Add to get \(\tfrac74u\cos\alpha=3V\). Since \(\cos\alpha=4/5\), \(u=15V/7\) and \(w=-2V/7\). The transverse component stays \(u\sin\alpha=9V/7\); hence the final speed is \(V\sqrt{85}/7\).

(b) The outgoing component along the centres is negative. Its acute angle to the backward direction satisfies \(\tan\theta=(9V/7)/(2V/7)=9/2\). The deflection is \(180^\circ-\theta-\alpha=65.7^\circ\).

A smooth uniform sphere S, of mass m, is moving on a smooth horizontal plane when it collides obliquely with another smooth uniform sphere T, of the same radius as S but of mass 2m, which is at rest on the plane. Immediately before the collision the velocity of S makes an angle \(\alpha\), where tan \(\alpha=\frac{3}{4}\), with the line joining the centres of the spheres.\par Immediately after the collision the speed of T is V. The coefficient of restitution between the two spheres is \(\frac{3}{4}\).\par (a) Find, in terms of V, the speed of S\par (i) immediately before the collision,\par (ii) immediately after the collision.\par (b) Find the angle through which the direction of motion of S is deflected as a result of the collision.\par

(a) T starts at rest and finishes at speed \(V\), so it receives an impulse \(2mV\) along the centres. The opposite impulse changes S’s normal component from \(p=u\cos\alpha\) to \(p-2V\). Restitution gives \(V-(p-2V)=3p/4\). Thus \(p=12V/7\) and \(u=p/(4/5)=15V/7\). The transverse component is \(p\tan\alpha=9V/7\), so the outgoing speed is \(V\sqrt{(-2)^2+9^2}/7=V\sqrt{85}/7\).

(b) Use the scalar product of the incident and outgoing direction vectors. They are proportional to \((12,9)\) and \((-2,9)\), respectively. Thus \(\cos\delta=(-24+81)/(15\sqrt{85})\), giving \(\delta=65.7^\circ\).
